links.outcome: ChatGPT-4o accuracy on Letournel-Judet acetabular fracture classification versus residents
links.effect: Overall accuracy 17.9% for ChatGPT-4o vs 88.6% and 91.8% for the two residents; kappa with reference standard -0.014 for ChatGPT-4o.
links.quote: The overall diagnostic accuracy for the final Letournel-Judet classification was 17.9% for ChatGPT-4o, compared to 88.6% and 91.8% for the first and second orthopaedic residents, respectively.

links.outcome: Comparison of AI classification performance against clinicians on same radiographs
links.effect: Both residents performed significantly better than ChatGPT-4o (p<0.001); residents' kappa 0.860 and 0.900 vs -0.014 for the AI.
links.quote: Both residents performed significantly better than the AI model (p< 0.001), with no significant difference observed between the residents (p= 0.070).

screen.reason: Empirical study evaluating the diagnostic reliability of a multimodal foundation model (ChatGPT-4o) compared to orthopaedic residents on retrospective pelvic radiographs.
